summary: switchPack has no concurrency guard: two overlapping calls leave an orphaned second disc in the scene forever (double-rendered artwork + GPU leak) and desync `current` from the pack dropdown.
scenario: Operator picks pack B in the dropdown while pack A (e.g. live-2000, 2.7M events, plus the 600ms retry sleep) is still awaiting loadPack. Call A nulled `current` on entry, so call B skips removal; whichever load finishes LAST wins `current` and calls hud.setPack, while the other finished disc was already scene.add()ed and is never removed or disposed. Both discs render additively on top of each other (visibly corrupt artwork); millions of grain/stroke vertices leak in VRAM; if A finishes last the dropdown even snaps back to A while discB stays superimposed. Same race fires when handleLive COMPLETE auto-calls switchPack(packName) while the operator touches the dropdown, or when the user changes packs during the initial switchPack(PACKS[0]).
fix_sketch: Token-guard the async section: `const tok = ++switchSeq;` before `await loadPack`, and after the await `if (tok !== switchSeq) return;` (also re-check before scene.add / current assignment). Alternatively disable the pack select while a load is in flight.
repro_evidence: Code reading of main.js lines 92-116: `current` is removed and nulled before the await at line 98; scene.add + `current = {...}` happen unconditionally after the await, so interleavings provably add two disc groups while only one is tracked.

summary: pickLane's 1.2*laneWidth acceptance radius reaches 0.7 laneWidths into the 2-laneWidth zone gaps, so ~70% of the gap area selects an edge seat instead of returning null as the function's contract ('null ... in a gap') states.
scenario: Operator clicks in the separator ring between zone A and zone B intending to deselect (the documented gap behavior): anywhere in the first or last 35% of the gap, pickLane returns the adjacent zone's edge lane (verified: 10% and 35% into the gap return lane 63, 90% returns lane 64) and the seat panel pops up for a seat the operator did not click; only the middle 30% of the gap deselects.
fix_sketch: Clamp acceptance to the zone band: accept only if r is within [band.r0, band.r1] of the picked lane's band (zoneBands are already computed), or drop the tolerance to <= 0.6*laneWidth.

summary: During live recording, pressing Space (or Enter) activates the still-focused KAYIT button and silently stops the 90s take early; the space guard only protects pack mode.
scenario: Operator clicks '● KAYIT' to start a take — in Chromium the button keeps focus. Mid-take the operator hits Space out of replay muscle-memory (or Enter). The window keydown handler at main.js:85 only calls preventDefault when `current` is non-null, and in live mode `current` is null, so the browser's default action fires: the focused rec button is clicked -> onRecord -> live is set -> stopRecording() -> POST /api/stop -> the recorder aborts and finalizes. The one-shot audience take is truncated on disk with zero confirmation. (Enter activates on keydown and is never guarded, so it also toggles record/stop in pack mode.)
fix_sketch: In hud.js, blur after click (`$('rec').onclick = (e) => { e.currentTarget.blur(); onRecord(); }` — same for all buttons), and/or extend the keydown guard: `if (e.key === ' ') { e.preventDefault(); if (current) togglePlay(); }`. Consider requiring a confirm (double-press) to stop an active recording.
repro_evidence: Code reading: main.js:83-90 (guard `e.key === ' ' && current`), main.js:47 onRecord toggles stop when live, hud.js:48 rec button click wiring; standard Chromium focus/space-activation behavior.

summary: A clean upstream close (FIN from a proxy idle-timeout or upstream restart) hits `return; // clean end of stream` and never reconnects, so the recorder finalizes the 90s session immediately with whatever it has — a silently truncated one-shot live recording marked COMPLETE.
scenario: Show is running, session started for 90s; 20s in, the venue proxy or upstream SSE server closes the connection cleanly (FIN, no error). liveSource returns instead of retrying, recordFromSource's for-await ends, session.stop()/finalize() run, the server broadcasts COMPLETE and auto-packs a 20s recording. The comment on the generator ('Reconnects with backoff') and the killer-timeout comment in server.js both assume the source survives disconnects — only error closes actually reconnect.
fix_sketch: In the clean-end path, only return when `signal?.aborted`; otherwise fall through to the same backoff/retry logic as the catch branch (a clean end mid-session is a disconnect, not end-of-show). Keep maxRetries:0 single-shot semantics for tests.
repro_evidence: tmp-repro/repro-clean-close.mjs: local SSE server sends 2 events then res.end() at 300ms; recordFromSource({durationMs:90000, stopAfterMs:90000}) returned after 311 ms with session state COMPLETE, stats {received:2, stored:2}.
reasoning: Code reading confirms live-source.js line 28 unconditionally returns when the fetch body iteration ends without error, and the reconnect/backoff logic exists only in the catch branch — so only error closes reconnect; a clean upstream close (res.end()/terminal chunk, which undici surfaces as a clean end of body iteration, not an error) permanently ends the generator. recorder.js then exits its for-await, runs session.stop()/finalize(), and server.js broadcasts COMPLETE and auto-packs. Runtime repro (tmp-repro/repro-clean-close.mjs): a local SSE server sending 2 events then res.end() at 300ms caused recordFromSource({durationMs:90000, stopAfterMs:90000}) with default maxRetries:Infinity to resolve after 312ms with session state COMPLETE — a silently truncated 90s live recording marked successful. The generator's own comment ('Reconnects with backoff'), the Infinity default, and server.js's killer-timeout comment all show the live path was meant to survive disconnects, so this is a genuine defect, and critical for a one-shot live show recording.
corrected_fix: In live-source.js, replace the unconditional clean-end `return` (line 28): after the body iteration ends, return only if `signal?.aborted` or `maxRetries === 0` (preserving single-shot test semantics); otherwise treat the clean end as a disconnect and fall through to the same retry accounting as the catch branch (increment retries, respect the maxRetries cap, sleep with exponential backoff, reconnect). Optionally also reset the retry counter — not just the delay — after a successful connect so a long-running show doesn't exhaust retries across many reconnects.

summary: The live disc is built from the PREVIOUS session's roster (stale hello roster) and ensureLiveDisc's early-return then ignores every genuine roster broadcast, so new-session participants beyond the 64 spare lanes are silently invisible.
scenario: Operator does a small soundcheck recording (e.g. 3 tech seats), then arms the real 2000-person show. server.js never clears latestRoster between sessions and includes it in the /api/live hello even in ARMED state (proven: hello.state=ARMED, hello.roster=[A1,A2,A3] from the finished session). main.js:170 calls ensureLiveDisc(msg.roster) without checking msg.state, locking the layout to the soundcheck roster; when the real session's roster broadcast arrives, ensureLiveDisc returns at `if (live.disc) return;` (main.js:146). Everyone not in the stale roster funnels through rosterLayout's 64 spare lanes and then laneOf() returns null — processLiveEvents drops their events. Proven: 136 of 200 fresh participants dropped. Same lock-in via the >12000-queued-events derived-roster path (main.js:176-184), which at the real 31k events/s fires ~0.4s in, likely before the first snapshot. The JSONL/pack is fine; the live artwork the audience watches is missing most of the crowd.
fix_sketch: In the hello handler, only trust msg.roster when msg.state === 'RECORDING'. On a 'roster' message, if the current layout came from a stale/derived roster (or roster size grew materially), rebuild layout+disc and replay a kept event buffer. Server-side companion fix: reset latestRoster = null in POST /api/start.
repro_evidence: tmp-repro/repro-stale-roster-and-stop409.mjs → 'hello.state = ARMED, hello.roster = [{A,1},{A,2},{A,3}] ... PROOF A CONFIRMED'; tmp-repro/repro-spare-overflow.mjs (imports the real rosterLayout/buildLayout) → 'placed=64 dropped=136 CONFIRMED'.
reasoning: Verified by reading src/server.js (latestRoster lifecycle, hello payload, /api/start), viz/src/main.js (hello/roster/batch handlers, ensureLiveDisc early-return, processLiveEvents null-lane drop), and viz/src/live-disc.js (rosterLayout 64 spare lanes, laneOf null overflow), and by running both cited tmp-repro scripts against the real modules: repro-stale-roster-and-stop409.mjs printed 'hello.state = ARMED', 'hello.roster = [A1,A2,A3]', 'PROOF A ... CONFIRMED'; repro-spare-overflow.mjs printed 'placed=64 dropped=136 ... CONFIRMED'.
corrected_fix: Server (src/server.js): in POST /api/start, reset `latestRoster = null` before starting the new session, so a hello during ARMED/early-RECORDING never carries a previous session's roster. Client (viz/src/main.js): in the hello handler, ignore `msg.roster` unless `msg.state === 'RECORDING'` (defense in depth); and in the `kind:'roster'` handler, instead of relying on ensureLiveDisc's early-return, detect when the incoming roster materially outgrows the current layout (or when the layout came from the derived-roster fallback) and rebuild: keep a running buffer of all appended events, dispose the old disc, build the new rosterLayout/createLiveDisc, and replay the buffer through processLiveEvents. Cheapest safe variant if replay memory is a concern at 2.7M events: rebuild only on the first genuine roster after a stale/derived layout, which at 40ms batch cadence happens within the first seconds while the buffer is still small.

summary: commit() permanently loses GPU uploads when it runs more than once between two renders: each commit calls attr.clearUpdateRanges(), wiping the previous commit's not-yet-flushed update range, while dirtyFrom has already advanced so the lost range is never re-sent.
scenario: main.js processLiveEvents (line 162) calls live.disc.commit() once per SSE 'batch' message, not once per frame as live-disc's contract comment requires. Three r185 only consumes updateRanges at render time (WebGLAttributes.update is version-gated; updateBuffer uploads the listed ranges then clears them). Whenever two 40ms batches land between two rAF ticks — a frame that takes >40ms under the ~31k events/s peak, or the operator switching to the control-panel tab so rAF pauses while EventSource keeps delivering — the second commit's clearUpdateRanges() discards the first batch's range. Those grains stay zeros on the GPU forever but are inside drawRange: aR=0/aT=0/aLane=0 points render as an ever-brighter additive blob at the disc center at 12 o'clock, and the real grains are missing from the spiral for the rest of the show. After a minute in a hidden tab, nearly everything appended meanwhile is corrupted.
repro_evidence: node tmp-repro/commit-range-loss.mjs (uses the real createLiveDisc + three r185 BufferAttribute and replays WebGLAttributes.updateBuffer semantics copied from node_modules/three/src/renderers/webgl/WebGLAttributes.js): prints 'elements whose CPU value never reached the GPU: 100; gpu aT[100..104] = 0,0,0,0,0 (expected 2000..2004)' with drawRange.count=300. Verified in three source that updateBuffer clears ranges only when it actually uploads, and update() is gated on data.version < attribute.version.
fix_sketch: In commit(), stop calling clearUpdateRanges() — just addUpdateRange for the new span and set needsUpdate; the renderer merges overlapping/adjacent ranges and clears them after upload. (Or, equivalently, move the single commit() call into the rAF loop right before renderer.render, per the function's own 'call once per frame' comment.)
reasoning: Verified by reading all three load-bearing pieces and running the repro. (1) main.js:162 calls live.disc.commit() once per SSE 'batch' message inside processLiveEvents; renderer.render happens only in the rAF frame() loop, which never calls commit — so multiple commits between two renders occur whenever a frame exceeds 40ms or the tab is hidden (rAF pauses, EventSource keeps firing). (2) live-disc.js:83 commit() calls attr.clearUpdateRanges() before adding its own range and then advances dirtyFrom=count, so a wiped span is never re-marked; append() only lowers dirtyFrom (never happens since count is monotonic), making the loss permanent. (3) three 0.185.1 node_modules/three/src/renderers/webgl/WebGLAttributes.js confirms uploads are version-gated and happen only at render time (update: data.version < attribute.version), updateBuffer uploads exactly the listed updateRanges then clears them itself, and createBuffer uploads the full array on a chunk's first render. Ran node tmp-repro/commit-range-loss.mjs (real createLiveDisc + real three BufferAttribute, gl mock replaying r185 updateBuffer semantics verbatim): drawRange.count=300, 100 elements never reach the GPU, gpu aT[100..104]=0 (expected 2000..2004). Shader check confirms the artifact: lost grains (aR=0,aT=0,aKind=0) are inside drawRange, visible (uTime>0), positioned at the disc center, additively blended — a brightening center blob plus missing real grains, and they also flare when lane 0 is selected (aLane=0). Two minor overstatements, neither load-bearing: chunks created entirely while hidden take the createBuffer full-array path on return and are correct, so hidden-tab loss is bounded by the un-flushed remainder of chunks already on the GPU (~up to 131k grains each) rather than literally everything; and 'at 12 o'clock' is moot since aR=0 places points exactly at the center. Recorded JSONL/pack data is unaffected — corruption is confined to the live view — but the live render is the on-stage artwork during recording, so critical severity stands.
corrected_fix: In live-disc.js commit(), remove the attr.clearUpdateRanges() call — just addUpdateRange(chunk.dirtyFrom, chunk.count - chunk.dirtyFrom) and set needsUpdate: three r185's updateBuffer sorts, merges overlapping/adjacent ranges, uploads them, and clears the list itself after upload (verified in node_modules/three/src/renderers/webgl/WebGLAttributes.js), so accumulated ranges from multiple commits between renders are all flushed. Equivalently (and matching the function's own 'call once per frame' contract comment), move the single commit() call out of processLiveEvents in main.js and into the rAF frame() loop right before view.renderer.render when live?.disc is set. Either change alone fixes the loss; doing both is harmless.

summary: ingest only rejects tMs > durationMs, never tMs < 0, so any event whose server timestamp precedes the anchor (first stored event) is recorded with a negative tMs — and packSession then crashes with RangeError at events.writeUInt32LE (viz-pack.js:75), making the whole recording unpackable.
scenario: Live feed at ~31k events/s: the first stored event anchors the clock; any event from another upstream worker/shard whose ts is even 1 ms earlier yields tMs = -1, which session.ingest accepts and the recorder writes to JSONL. After the 90 s take, server autopack calls packSession, writeUInt32LE(-1) throws, the .catch in server.js:108-113 sets phase IDLE and broadcasts 'recording failed' — the operator is told the show take failed (it is actually on disk) and gets no pack; the CLI pack of the same file crashes identically, so the recording is unrenderable without hand-editing. Non-integer ts (Number.isFinite allows floats) produces fractional tMs and the same throw.
fix_sketch: In session.ingest treat tMs < 0 explicitly (clamp to 0, or re-anchor anchorServerMs = min(anchor, ts) — rejecting loses real audience data); additionally make viz-pack defensive: write Math.max(0, Math.min(durationMs, Math.round(tMs))) so an already-recorded file still packs. Note the events.bin 'sorted (lane,tMs)' header comment is also untrue for out-of-order ts since per-lane order is arrival order.
repro_evidence: tmp-repro/repro-negative-tms.js: ingest of ts=999999 after anchor ts=1000000 returned {accepted:true, tMs:-1}; packSession on the resulting JSONL threw RangeError 'must be >= 0 and <= 4294967295. Received -1'.
reasoning: Verified by reading and by tmp-repro (tmp-repro/repro-negative-tms.js). session.js:50-52 anchors the clock on the first stored event and only rejects tMs > durationMs, so an event with an earlier server ts is accepted with negative tMs — repro returned {accepted:true, tMs:-1}. recorder.js/jsonl.js write that record verbatim to the JSONL. viz-pack.js:75 then throws RangeError at events.writeUInt32LE(-1) — repro reproduced the exact throw ('must be >= 0 and <= 4294967295. Received -1'), making the whole recording unpackable via both the server auto-pack and the CLI. server.js:92-113 awaits packSession inside record.then, so the throw lands in the .catch which sets phase IDLE and broadcasts 'recording failed' even though the JSONL take completed successfully on disk, and lastSummary is never set. Nothing in the repo validates upstream ts monotonicity (adapter.js:17 accepts any finite ts), and a single 1 ms reorder relative to the very first stored event anywhere in a ~2.7M-event take fires the crash. One secondary detail is wrong: on Node 22, writeUInt32LE silently truncates in-range floats (0.5 -> 0, verified), so non-integer ts causes silent quantization, not the claimed throw; only negative/out-of-range values throw. The side note about the 'sorted (lane,tMs)' header comment being untrue for out-of-order ts is accurate (per-lane records are written in arrival order). The core claim, failure scenario, crash site, and operator-facing consequence are all correct.
corrected_fix: In session.ingest (src/session.js:52), handle tMs < 0 explicitly instead of silently accepting it: either clamp to 0 or re-anchor (anchorServerMs = Math.min(anchorServerMs, ev.serverTimestampMs)) so early-stamped audience events are kept rather than dropped. Independently harden the packer so already-recorded takes remain packable: in src/viz-pack.js write Math.max(0, Math.min(durationMs, Math.round(tMs))) at line 75 (and the same clamp for stroke t0/t1 at lines 103-104). Correction to the claim's fix rationale: fractional tMs does not throw on Node 22 (writeUInt32LE truncates in-range floats), but Math.round is still worthwhile to avoid silent truncation drift. Also fix or implement the 'sorted (lane, tMs)' promise in the events.bin header comment, since per-lane order is arrival order.

summary: A clean upstream end-of-stream mid-recording ends the recording silently instead of reconnecting: `return; // clean end of stream` bypasses the retry loop entirely, so the reconnect/backoff machinery only ever runs for thrown errors.
scenario: Operator starts a 90s live recording (panel /api/start or `cli.js record-live`). 20s in, a proxy idle-timeout, venue-engine restart, or LB drain closes the SSE response cleanly (no error). liveSource returns, recorder's for-await ends, session.stop()/finalize() run, the JSONL gets a normal end line, server.js broadcasts COMPLETE and auto-packs. The operator gets a truncated 20s session presented as a fully successful recording — no error, no reconnect attempt, and nothing in the file marks it as cut short. SSE clients are expected to reconnect on stream end (EventSource always does); with maxRetries defaulting to Infinity the code's own intent is 'keep going', but a clean close defeats it.
repro_evidence: tmp-repro/clean-close.mjs: SSE server writes 3 events then res.end(). recordFromSource with durationMs/stopAfterMs 90000 resolved with {intendedMs:90000, actualElapsedMs:12, events:3, upstreamConnects:1, finalState:"COMPLETE"} — 90s recording ended after 12ms, zero reconnect attempts, finalized as COMPLETE.
fix_sketch: Treat a clean close the same as a disconnect while a signal-less/unaborted consumer still wants data: replace `return` with `continue` into the backoff path (reset nothing on clean close, or apply backoff), and only `return` when `signal?.aborted` or maxRetries is exhausted. Keep a `maxRetries: 0` escape for the single-shot test mode.
reasoning: Reading /Users/mehmetunal/Documents/CluadeCodeFiles/2000-traces/src/sources/live-source.js confirms the mechanism exactly as claimed: the reconnect loop can only re-iterate through the catch block, so line 28's `return; // clean end of stream` terminates the generator on any clean upstream close, even with the default maxRetries=Infinity and an unaborted signal. A tmp-repro (tmp-repro/clean-close-verify.mjs: SSE server writes events then res.end() during a durationMs=90000 recording) resolved in 10ms with {upstreamConnects: 1, finalState: "COMPLETE"} — zero reconnect attempts. Downstream, recorder.js treats source-end as recording-end (session.stop()/finalize(), normal end line written), and server.js's .then path auto-packs and broadcasts COMPLETE with no truncation marker, so the panel presents a cut-short capture as fully successful. server.js line 201 passes no maxRetries override, so the code's own default (Infinity) states an intent to keep reconnecting that a clean close silently defeats; clean SSE stream ends are routine (proxy idle timeouts, LB drains, upstream graceful restarts — only abrupt res.destroy() throws into the retry path, as the existing 'reconnects after a dropped connection' test shows). Severity critical is justified: this tool records an unrepeatable live audience performance, and the failure is silent data loss mislabeled as COMPLETE.
corrected_fix: In live-source.js, treat a clean end-of-stream like a disconnect while the consumer still wants data: instead of `return` at line 28, check `if (signal?.aborted) return;` and `if (retries >= maxRetries) return;` (return, not throw — there is no error object on a clean close; this also preserves the maxRetries:0 single-shot behavior the tests at test/live-source.test.js:31,59 rely on, and the maxRetries:1 reconnect test still terminates because retries is already exhausted when its second connection ends cleanly). Otherwise increment retries, await the backoff delay, and continue the loop. Optionally, recorder.js/server.js could additionally record whether the session ended by duration/operator stop versus source exhaustion so a truncated capture is distinguishable in the JSONL/status, but the live-source change alone restores the intended reconnect-forever behavior for the control server's default configuration.

summary: Every take after the first builds the live disc from the PREVIOUS take's roster: /api/live hello sends the never-cleared latestRoster, the viz builds the disc from it immediately, and ensureLiveDisc ignores the fresh roster broadcast that follows.
scenario: Take 1 completes; the audience changes (new show, different seats). Operator presses KAYIT for take 2: startRecording arms, connects EventSource, and the hello frame carries take 1's roster (server.js:135, latestRoster is only set on snapshot at :85 and never reset between sessions). main.js:170 `if (msg.roster?.length) ensureLiveDisc(msg.roster)` builds the live layout from the stale roster. When the new upstream snapshot arrives seconds later, the 'roster' broadcast hits ensureLiveDisc which early-returns because live.disc already exists (main.js:147). Result: departed participants keep empty dedicated lanes; genuinely new (z,s) pairs are shunted into the 64 spare lanes and, past 64, laneOf returns null and their events are silently dropped from the projected artwork (main.js:160). Only a server restart clears it — a page reload does not.
fix_sketch: Server: reset `latestRoster = null` on /api/start (or on session completion), and stamp roster frames with the sessionId. Viz: rebuild the live disc when a 'roster' message arrives for the current session and the existing layout was derived from a stale/hello roster (or don't build from hello.roster when state is IDLE/ARMED/COMPLETE — wait for the session's own snapshot).
repro_evidence: Ran tmp-repro/stale-roster.mjs: after take 1 COMPLETE, a fresh /api/live connection's hello frame contained roster [{"z":"A","s":1},{"z":"A","s":2}] from the finished take. Viz-side chain confirmed by reading main.js:167-171, 146-154 and live-disc.js:104-128.
reasoning: Verified by reading all four files and by running a repro against the real server (tmp-repro/stale-roster-verify.mjs, using the actual createControlServer + recorder). (1) Server: latestRoster is assigned only in the onSnapshot tap (server.js:85) and never cleared — not on /api/start, completion, or error; the /api/live hello (server.js:135) sends it unconditionally. Repro output: after take 1 (roster A1/A2) reached COMPLETE, arming take 2 and connecting /api/live returned hello {state:"ARMED", roster:[{"z":"A","s":1},{"z":"A","s":2}]} — the previous take's roster — and the correct take-2 roster (B5/B6) arrived only in the later 'roster' broadcast after /api/start. (2) Viz: startRecording (main.js:119) creates live with disc:null, arms, connects; the hello handler builds the disc from the stale roster (main.js:170) before posting /api/start (main.js:171); ensureLiveDisc early-returns once live.disc exists (main.js:146-147), so the fresh 'roster' broadcast (main.js:173-174) is a no-op. (3) Consequence: rosterLayout (live-disc.js:104-128) dedicates lanes to stale members (empty ghost lanes for departed seats); new (z,s) keys consume the 64 spare lanes and past 64 laneOf returns null (live-disc.js:122), and processLiveEvents drops those events (main.js:159-160). At ~2000 participants, >64 new identities between takes is realistic, so a changed audience's live projection is largely blank/mislaid, silently, while recording continues. Page reload does not clear it (server memory); only server restart does. Mitigations that keep this from being data loss: the JSONL recording and auto-packed final artwork are correct — only the live 90s view is wrong, and takes with an unchanged audience are unaffected. Severity 'critical' stands because the live view is the audience-facing projection during a show, the failure is silent, affects every take after the first once the audience churns, and has no in-app recovery.
corrected_fix: Server: clear the stale roster at session end (set latestRoster = null in the record completion/catch handlers in server.js, or at /api/arm) rather than at /api/start — the viz sequence is arm → connect → hello → start, so a reset only in /api/start still leaves the stale roster in the ARMED hello. Optionally stamp roster/hello frames with sessionId. Viz: in main.js, only build the disc from hello.roster when hello.state === 'RECORDING' (mid-take reconnect); when ARMED, wait for the session's own 'roster' broadcast (the existing >12000-event queue fallback already covers a missing snapshot). Alternatively/additionally, let a 'roster' message rebuild a hello-derived layout, replaying live.queue plus already-appended events into the new disc.

summary: The single .catch covers auto-pack as well as recording: if packSession throws, a fully successful recording is reported to the operator as 'recording failed', phase goes to IDLE (never COMPLETE), lastSummary is never set, and the error itself is discarded with no diagnostics.
scenario: Recording completes normally (valid JSONL with end line on disk), but packSession fails (packs dir unwritable/missing parent, disk full, corrupt line). The .then rejects at `await packSession(...)`, the .catch broadcasts {state:'IDLE', error:'recording failed'} and /api/status thereafter shows state IDLE, stats null, sessionId null. The operator believes the take was lost and may panic or re-run; the COMPLETE broadcast never fires so a live viewer waiting on it hangs; the actual error is swallowed (`.catch(() => ...)`).
fix_sketch: Wrap only `await packSession(...)` in its own try/catch: on pack failure still set lastSummary (packName:null, packError:message) and phase='COMPLETE', broadcasting COMPLETE with a packError field. Reserve the outer .catch for genuine record failures, and include err.message in the broadcast/status plus a console.error.
repro_evidence: tmp-repro/repro-autopack-failure.mjs: packsDir nested under a regular file. Output: JSONL last line kind 'end' with stats {received:2, stored:2} (recording complete on disk), but broadcasts ended with {state:'IDLE', error:'recording failed'} and /api/status = {state:'IDLE', stats:null, sessionId:null, packName:null}.
reasoning: Verified by code reading and a runnable repro. recorder.js resolves the record promise only after the JSONL end line is written and the stream finishes, so the take is fully on disk when server.js's .then runs. The `await packSession(...)` at server.js:102 sits inside that .then, and viz-pack.js has real post-recording throw paths (mkdirSync of outDir, writeFileSync ENOSPC, JSON.parse of a corrupt line). Any such throw rejects the .then and lands in the single argument-less .catch at line 108, which sets phase='IDLE', never sets lastSummary, broadcasts {state:'IDLE', error:'recording failed'}, and swallows the error with no logging. Repro (tmp-repro/repro-autopack-failure.mjs, packsDir nested under a regular file) produced exactly the claimed outcome: JSONL last line kind 'end' with stats {received:2, stored:2}, participants:1, but broadcasts ended with {"state":"IDLE","error":"recording failed"} (COMPLETE never fired) and /api/status returned {"state":"IDLE","stats":null,"sessionId":null,"packName":null}. Additional wrinkle: on a non-first run, stale lastSummary from the previous session leaks into /api/status, which is even more misleading. Severity 'important' is right: the JSONL take survives on disk (recoverable via /api/sessions), so no data loss, but a false 'recording failed' during a one-shot live-audience take is a serious operator hazard and live viewers waiting on COMPLETE hang.
corrected_fix: In server.js's .then, wrap only the pack step in its own try/catch: `let packError = null; if (autoPack && packsDir && summary.participants > 0) { packName = sessionId.replace(/^session-/, 'kayit-'); try { await packSession(outPath, join(packsDir, packName)); } catch (err) { packError = err?.message ?? String(err); packName = null; console.error('auto-pack failed:', err); } }` then still set `lastSummary = { ...summary, sessionId, packName, packError }`, set phase='COMPLETE', and include packError in the COMPLETE broadcast (and optionally in /api/status via lastSummary). Give the outer .catch an `(err)` parameter, log it with console.error, and include err.message in the IDLE broadcast so genuine record failures are diagnosable.

summary: lastSummary = { ...summary, ... } retains the live `session` object that recordFromSource returns (recorder.js:58 `return { ...summary, outPath, session }`), pinning the entire in-memory event store and lastStored map of the finished session for as long as the server idles — ~90MB per 400k events, roughly 600MB for a 2.7M-event show session.
scenario: A full 2.7M-event session completes; the operator leaves the panel idle. The whole store stays resident (status() only reads stats/participants scalars from it — pure waste). When the next session starts, its own store grows to another ~600MB alongside the pinned one, plus any live-client buffering: peak memory roughly doubles per session and the recorder box can OOM mid-show, killing the recording process.
fix_sketch: Strip the heavy fields before storing: `const { session: _s, ...light } = summary; lastSummary = { ...light, sessionId, packName };` (or have recordFromSource not spread `session` into the summary and pass it only via onSession).
repro_evidence: tmp-repro scripts (inline node --expose-gc run): heapUsed 6.2MB baseline -> 95.3MB after a 400k-event session COMPLETE and gc (server idle, current=null) -> back to 7.6MB the moment a tiny second session replaces lastSummary. The +89MB is attributable solely to lastSummary retention.
reasoning: Verified by code reading plus an independent tmp-repro. recorder.js:58 resolves with `{ ...summary, outPath, session }` (session is an explicit property, not spread — minor phrasing nit in the claim). server.js:95 nulls `current`, then line 104 `lastSummary = { ...summary, sessionId, packName }` copies the `session` reference, making lastSummary the sole strong reference to the finished session's entire store (events array, byParticipant map, lastStored map). Grep confirms `lastSummary.session` is never read anywhere; status() consumes only stats/participants/sessionId/packName scalars, so the retention is pure waste. Independent measurement (tmp-repro/verify2.mjs, node --expose-gc, real recordFromSource over a synthetic 400k-event / 2000-participant source): idle heap 85.6 MB with the current server.js:104 shape vs 4.0 MB with session stripped — ~82 MB (~205 B/event) attributable solely to the pin, extrapolating to ~550 MB at the 2.7M-event show scale, matching the claim's numbers. The peak-doubling scenario is also correct: lastSummary is only replaced at the NEXT session's completion, so the old full store stays resident alongside the new growing store for the whole next recording. The only soft spot is the OOM tail — ~1.1 GB of stores alone likely fits Node 22's default old-space on typical hardware — but combined with 31k ev/s ingest, live SSE client buffering, and packSession at completion, the wasted memory materially erodes headroom on the process whose death kills the recording. Severity 'important' stands. The recorder's returned `session` is intentional API (test/acceptance.test.js:30 uses summary.session.store), so the server-side strip is the correct fix.
corrected_fix: In /Users/mehmetunal/Documents/CluadeCodeFiles/2000-traces/src/server.js line 104, strip the heavy session reference before storing: `const { session: _session, ...light } = summary; lastSummary = { ...light, sessionId, packName };`. This keeps every field status() and the COMPLETE broadcast need (stats, participants, sessionId, packName) while letting the finished session's store be garbage-collected. Do NOT remove `session` from recordFromSource's return value — test/acceptance.test.js:30 (`summary.session.store`) and the onSession-less CLI path rely on that API; the fix belongs in server.js only.

summary: broadcast() ignores res.write()'s return value and the hub has no drain handling, no per-client buffer cap, and no slow-client disconnect, so one stalled /api/live viewer (closed TCP window: lid closed, wifi drop without FIN — req 'close' fires only much later on retransmit timeout) buffers every frame in server memory without bound for the rest of the session.
scenario: During a show at ~31k events/s, a viewer laptop sleeps without sending FIN. Every 40ms flush keeps writing batches into that dead ServerResponse; measured ~31MB buffered per 400k events per stalled client, i.e. ~200MB+ over a 2.7M-event session per stalled viewer — stacked on the session store this can OOM the recorder process mid-recording.
fix_sketch: In broadcast, check the write() return / res.writableLength per client; when a client exceeds a small high-water mark (e.g. 1-2MB), destroy its response and delete it from liveClients (a live view can rejoin; it does not need history). Optionally also set a socket timeout on /api/live connections.
repro_evidence: tmp-repro/repro-stalled-client.mjs (node --expose-gc): raw socket sends GET /api/live then pause()s. 400k-event session: heapUsed delta 123.0MB vs 91.7MB in an identical run with no client — ~31MB of frames buffered for the single stalled client (remainder is the lastSummary retention bug).
reasoning: Verified by code reading and a runnable repro. In src/server.js broadcast() (lines 27-30) calls res.write(frame) for every client in liveClients and discards the return value; there is no drain handling, no writableLength/high-water check, no socket timeout (Node http default timeout is disabled; requestTimeout only covers request receipt, instant for a GET), and no heartbeat. A client is removed only on req 'close' (line 138), which for a peer that dies without FIN fires only after the TCP retransmission timeout (minutes), and for a zero-window stall may never fire. The pendingBatch>50000 drop valve (line 32) only applies when liveClients is empty, so one stalled client keeps every 40ms batch flowing into its buffered ServerResponse for the entire session. Repro (tmp-repro/repro-stalled-live-client.mjs): a raw socket sent GET /api/live, read the 311-byte hello, then pause()d; after a 200k-event synthetic session the server had buffered 13.0MB of frames for that client (all delivered immediately on resume; kernel loopback buffers are <1MB, so ~12.7MB+ sat in Node userland memory). Scaled to a real 2.7M-event session this is ~175-250MB per stalled viewer, stacked on the in-memory session store, in the same process doing the authoritative disk recording. Minor tempering nuance: the server binds 127.0.0.1 only, so the literal remote-laptop scenario needs a tunnel/forward, but any stalled reader (tunneled viewer, stalled or SIGSTOP'd local consumer) triggers the same unbounded growth, as reproduced. Severity 'important' is appropriate: requires a stalled client and the JSONL on disk survives a crash, but an OOM mid-show kills the recorder and truncates the capture. The proposed fix (per-client writableLength high-water mark in broadcast, destroy and remove offenders, optional socket timeout) is correct.

summary: pendingBatch is never reset at session boundaries — flushLive with zero clients keeps up to 50000 compacted events (and the .catch path never flushes or clears at all), so leftover events from a finished/failed session are broadcast into the next session's live stream; latestRoster similarly persists and is sent in 'hello' across sessions.
scenario: Session A runs with no viewer connected (events accumulate in pendingBatch; on completion flushLive() is a no-op because liveClients is empty). Operator arms and starts session B and a viewer connects: the first 40ms flush delivers session A's events — with A's tMs values and lanes — mixed into B's batch, drawing ghost strokes from the previous audience onto the new disc. Repro showed the B viewer receiving A's zone-A events alongside B's. Same leak after a failed session (catch clears nothing), where stale batches arrive after the {state:'IDLE'} broadcast.
fix_sketch: Reset hub state on session start (`pendingBatch = []; latestRoster = null;` in the /api/start handler before recordFromSource) and also clear pendingBatch in the .catch path; only broadcast roster/batches tagged with the current sessionId.
repro_evidence: tmp-repro/repro-pendingbatch-leak.mjs: VERDICT LEAK — viewer of session B received 2 events recorded in session A: [{z:'A',s:1,t:0,...},{z:'A',s:1,t:500,...}] in the same batch stream as B's {z:'B',s:9,...}.
reasoning: Verified by reading src/server.js and by a runtime repro (tmp-repro/verify-pendingbatch-leak.mjs). pendingBatch (server.js:24) is cleared only inside flushLive (lines 31-36) and only when liveClients is non-empty; with zero clients it is retained (dropped only when >50000). POST /api/start never resets it, the completion .then's flushLive() is a no-op with no clients, and the .catch path (lines 108-113) clears nothing. latestRoster is set only in onSnapshot (line 85), never cleared, and sent in every 'hello' (line 135). Batch frames carry no sessionId (line 35) and viz/src/main.js:175-186 appends all batch events unconditionally, so the client cannot filter. Repro: session A (zone A) recorded with no viewer, then session B started and a viewer connected — the viewer's hello contained A's stale roster [{z:'A',s:1}] and its first batch delivered A's two events (tMs 0 and 500) mixed with B's {z:'B',s:9} event. Exactly the claimed ghost-stroke scenario. Severity 'important' is appropriate: the authoritative on-disk recording and packs are unaffected; only the live re-broadcast view is polluted. The proposed fix (reset pendingBatch and latestRoster in /api/start, clear pendingBatch in .catch, tag frames with sessionId) is correct.

summary: If the recorder server dies mid-recording, the viz is permanently bricked in live mode: es.onerror only tears down when no disc exists yet, and there is no other exit path.
scenario: Recording is running (live.disc built, grains flowing). The panel process crashes or is Ctrl-C'd. EventSource fires onerror, but the guard `if (live && !live.disc)` skips stopLiveUi, so ES retries forever and `live` stays truthy. hud.setLiveMode(true) keeps play/restart/scrub/speed/final/export/pack disabled (hud.js:79-83), switchPack() returns early on `live` (main.js:93), and clicking KAYIT calls stopRecording() whose `fetch(/api/stop).catch(() => {})` swallows the network failure — no COMPLETE state will ever arrive to call stopLiveUi. The operator is stuck on a frozen counter with every control disabled; the only recovery is a full page reload, in front of a live audience.
fix_sketch: In es.onerror with a disc present, surface a reconnect/lost state instead of ignoring it; make stopRecording check for fetch failure (and non-ok status) and fall back to stopLiveUi('sunucu yanıt vermiyor') so a second KAYIT click always exits live mode.
repro_evidence: Code paths read and cross-checked: main.js:138 guard, main.js:93 switchPack guard, main.js:141-144 swallowed stop, hud.js:79-83 disabled controls. No state message can arrive with the server dead.
reasoning: Code reading confirms every link in the chain. main.js:138 — `es.onerror = () => { if (live && !live.disc) stopLiveUi(...) }` — is a no-op once the live disc exists (the normal mid-recording state), and EventSource retries a refused connection indefinitely, so onerror keeps firing into the skipped guard. stopLiveUi (the only code that resets `live` and re-enables the HUD) is called from exactly three sites: line 138 (guarded away), line 193 (COMPLETE state SSE message), line 203 (IDLE+error state SSE message); the latter two require a message from the dead server, which can never arrive. Clicking KAYIT while `live` is truthy routes to stopRecording (main.js:47), which sets "DURDURULUYOR…" and does `fetch(/api/stop).catch(() => {})` — the failure is swallowed, res.ok unchecked, `live` untouched. Meanwhile hud.setLiveMode(true) (hud.js:79-83) keeps play/restart/scrub/speed/final/export/pack disabled, switchPack returns early on `live` (main.js:93), space is gated on `current` (disposed at recording start, main.js:126), and window.__traces exposes only the ineffective stopRecording, not stopLiveUi. The frame loop keeps rendering with a frozen live.maxT counter. Only recovery is a page reload. Severity downgraded from critical to important: the trigger is the companion recorder process (same machine) crashing mid-recording — an external failure that already endangers the recording server-side regardless of the viz; recovery is one page reload with no viz-owned data lost; and the audience-facing disc keeps rendering (H hides the HUD), so it is an operator-control lockout with a fast workaround, not unrecoverable core breakage.
corrected_fix: Two changes in viz/src/main.js: (1) In es.onerror, when live.disc exists, surface the loss instead of ignoring it — e.g. hud.setRecState('■ BAĞLANTI KOPTU — yeniden deneniyor', true) and arm a one-shot timer (say 10 s) that calls stopLiveUi('kayıt sunucusuna ulaşılamıyor — kayıt yarıda kesildi') if no SSE message arrives before it fires (clear the timer in es.onmessage/handleLive). (2) Make stopRecording async and verify the stop actually reached the server: `try { const r = await fetch(`${RECORDER}/api/stop`, {method:'POST'}); if (!r.ok) throw 0; } catch { stopLiveUi('sunucu yanıt vermiyor — canlı mod kapatıldı'); }` so a KAYIT click always exits live mode even with the server dead. Optionally expose stopLiveUi on window.__traces as an emergency hatch.

summary: Double-clicking KAYIT starts two live flows: startRecording sets `live` only after `await fetch(/api/status)`, so a second click in that window opens a second EventSource — every event is then drawn twice and the first ES leaks forever.
scenario: onRecord (main.js:47) branches on `live`, which is assigned at main.js:128, after the awaited status fetch (main.js:121). Under render jank (2.7M-grain scenes) both click events of a double-click are delivered in a burst before the fetch resolves — or the single-threaded recorder at 31k ev/s answers /api/status slowly — so both calls pass the falsy check. Result: two `live` objects (second overwrites first), TWO EventSources whose onmessage both invoke handleLive on the shared module-level `live` — every 40ms batch is appended twice, doubling grain density/brightness and the HUD 'tane' counter for the whole session. stopLiveUi closes only live.es (the second); the orphaned first ES reconnects forever.
fix_sketch: Set a guard synchronously: `if (live || starting) return; starting = true;` at the top of startRecording (or assign a provisional `live` object before the first await), clearing it on every exit path.
repro_evidence: Code reading: main.js:47, 119-128, 135-137, 209. Both sockets receive every broadcast (server.js broadcast() writes to all liveClients) and handleLive uses the module-level `live`, not a captured one.
reasoning: Code reading plus a line-faithful Node repro (tmp-repro/double-record.mjs) confirm the race. main.js:47 branches on module-level `live`; `live` is assigned only at main.js:128, after `await fetch(/api/status)` at :121, so a second KAYIT click while the fetch is pending re-enters startRecording. hud.js:48 wires the rec button with no debounce, setRecState never disables it, setLiveMode's disable list excludes 'rec', and the first UI feedback (BAĞLANIYOR, main.js:130) appears only after the await — a slow /api/status (single-threaded recorder at 31k ev/s; auto-pack of ~2.7M events runs in the same process) shows no response to the first click and invites a second. Result: two EventSources, both registered in server.js liveClients (server.js:22-35,126-138 — broadcast writes every frame to all clients), both onmessage handlers invoking handleLive on the shared module-level `live`, so every batch is appended twice (repro: 10-event batch → 20 appends; doubled grain density and HUD counter). stopLiveUi (main.js:208) closes only live.es — exactly one of the two sockets; the orphan's onerror guard (`if (live && !live.disc)`, :138) is dead after live=null and EventSource auto-reconnects, so it leaks until page reload (repro: 1 socket still open after stop). Only nuances: the vulnerable window is precisely the status fetch (the arm await at :133 is after `live` is set), and "leaks forever" means until page reload. On-disk JSONL/pack remain correct (recorded server-side), so the corruption is confined to the live view — which is the artwork during the session — hence important, not critical.
corrected_fix: Add a synchronous re-entry guard in startRecording (viz/src/main.js:119): either a module-level flag — `if (live || starting) return; starting = true;` at the top, cleared on every exit path (the catch at :123, and once `live` is assigned at :128) — or assign a provisional `live` object synchronously before the first await (so onRecord routes subsequent clicks to stopRecording), resetting it to null in the recorder-down catch branch. Optionally also disable the rec button and show BAĞLANIYOR before the status fetch for user feedback.

summary: stopRecording (and the hello-handler's /api/start post) never checks the HTTP response: a stop during the ARMED window gets a 409 that is silently ignored, so the recording starts anyway after the operator 'stopped' it — and a failed start leaves the UI stuck on BAGLANIYOR/DURDURULUYOR with no recovery.
scenario: Operator clicks KAYIT, then immediately clicks again to cancel. The second click runs stopRecording while the server is still ARMED (viz posts /api/start only from the hello handler, main.js:171). POST /api/stop returns 409 {error:'not recording'} — proven — which stopRecording discards; the pending hello then posts /api/start and a full 90s recording runs that the operator believes was cancelled. Worse variant: the /api/start fetch itself fails (its `.catch(() => {})` swallows it), the server stays ARMED forever, no state event ever arrives, and the viz sits in live mode with every control disabled until a page reload.
fix_sketch: Await and inspect res.ok on both /api/stop and /api/start. On stop-409 while a start is pending, set a cancel flag the hello handler checks before posting start; on start failure, stopLiveUi('start basarisiz').
repro_evidence: tmp-repro/repro-stale-roster-and-stop409.mjs → 'stop while ARMED -> HTTP 409 {"error":"not recording"} ... PROOF B CONFIRMED'; server.js:117-121 (`if (!current) 409`) with current only set in POST /api/start.
reasoning: Verified by code reading and two repros against the real server. viz/src/main.js:141-144 stopRecording() posts /api/stop with only .catch(()=>{}), never reads the response, and never clears `live`; main.js:171 posts /api/start the same way. src/server.js:117-121 returns 409 {error:'not recording'} whenever `current` is null — which is exactly the ARMED phase, since `current` is only created in POST /api/start. End-to-end repro (tmp-repro/repro-stop409-recording-proceeds.mjs) replays the viz client's exact fetch ordering: arm → open /api/live → operator stop (409, silently ignored) → hello processed → /api/start (200) → recording runs to COMPLETE and writes a session file — the take the operator believed cancelled. The pre-existing tmp-repro/repro-stale-roster-and-stop409.mjs independently proves the 409. Nuances: the race window (stop landing between arm and the hello-driven start) is tens of ms on localhost — reachable via accidental double-click but narrow — and once the RECORDING broadcast flips the HUD to '■ KAYIT', a second stop click does work, so the phantom recording is recoverable if noticed. The stuck-forever-ARMED variant is real in code (hud.setLiveMode(true) disables every control except rec, which only re-fires the 409ing stop; es.onerror recovers only on an actual SSE connection failure with no disc) but requires the single /api/start fetch to fail at network level while the EventSource to the same host stays healthy — a start that 409s because another client won is followed by a RECORDING broadcast and the UI recovers. The core defect — both control POSTs discard non-2xx responses, so a cancel during ARMED silently does not cancel — genuinely occurs.
corrected_fix: In viz/src/main.js: (1) stopRecording: set a cancel flag on `live` (e.g. live.cancelling = true), then `const res = await fetch(RECORDER + '/api/stop', {method:'POST'})`; if `!res.ok` (409 = server not recording yet), keep the flag so the pending start is suppressed rather than pretending the stop succeeded. (2) handleLive hello branch (line 171): before posting /api/start, check `live.cancelling` — if set, skip the start and call stopLiveUi(null) to exit live mode; otherwise await the start and on `!res.ok` or fetch failure call stopLiveUi('kayıt başlatılamadı — panele bak') instead of swallowing the error. (3) Optionally have the server broadcast {kind:'state', state:'ARMED'-cancelled or 'IDLE'} on a stop-while-ARMED (or accept stop during ARMED by resetting phase to IDLE in server.js /api/stop), which removes the race at the source — the client-side flag alone already fixes the operator-facing bug without touching server files.

summary: switchPack has no reentrancy guard: overlapping calls each pass the 'if (current)' cleanup at entry, then both resolve and add their disc group to the scene — the earlier one becomes an orphan that is never removed or disposed and keeps rendering additively under the new disc.
scenario: Operator flips the HUD pack <select> twice quickly (each change fires switchPack; loading a ~2.7M-event pack over the dev server takes long enough to overlap), or the auto switchPack from the recording-COMPLETE handler (line 201) races an operator-initiated switch. Call B enters while call A is awaiting loadPack: current is null so B removes nothing; A resolves, adds disc A, sets current=A; B resolves, adds disc B, overwrites current=B. Disc A stays in view.scene forever — a double-exposed image (both discs additive-blend) and a leak of tens of MB of GPU buffers per occurrence; only a page reload recovers. The same race hits startRecording: hitting KAYIT while a switchPack load is in flight lets the pack disc land in the scene mid-recording and it renders behind the live disc.
repro_evidence: Code reading only: switchPack (main.js:92-116) checks/disposes current synchronously at entry, awaits loadPack, then unconditionally scene.add + current=... with no generation token; startRecording (119-139) has the same shape. Browser-only interleaving, not reproducible in node.
fix_sketch: Use a generation token: const gen = ++switchGen captured at entry; after each await, bail if gen !== switchGen (and if live became truthy). Dispose the freshly built disc when bailing. Apply the same check before scene.add in the COMPLETE handler.
reasoning: Code reading confirms every element, and a node reduction of the exact async control flow reproduces both interleavings. switchPack (viz/src/main.js:92-116) does cleanup only synchronously at entry, then awaits loadPack (plus a 600ms retry sleep at line 100 that widens the window), then unconditionally scene.add + current=... with no generation token and no post-await re-check of live. Overlapping calls: the second passes the entry cleanup as a no-op (current already null), both resolve, both add their disc group; the loser of the race stays in view.scene forever — never removed, never disposed. The orphan renders visibly, not just leaks: buildDisc initializes uTime to manifest.durationMs (disc.js:62), the shader shows all events via step(aT, uTime) (shaders.js:29), and both materials are AdditiveBlending with depthTest:false (disc.js:116,161), so the orphan additive-blends fully engraved under the new disc every frame; its buffers (~tens of MB at 2.7M events) are never freed. Triggers are real: hud.js disables the pack select only in live mode, not during loads; the COMPLETE handler (main.js:199-201) calls switchPack after live is cleared and can race an operator select. The startRecording race is also confirmed: switchPack checks live only at entry (line 93), startRecording sets live after its status-fetch await (lines 121-128), and the live render branch (main.js:244) renders the whole scene, so an in-flight pack load lands its disc mid-recording and it draws under the live disc. Repro: /Users/mehmetunal/Documents/CluadeCodeFiles/2000-traces/tmp-repro/switchpack-race.mjs (scene ends with both discs, zero disposals; recording case ends with pack disc in scene while live is active). One additional symptom beyond the claim: with reversed resolution order the older load wins current and hud.setPack, leaving the HUD/current on a pack the user did not last select — same root cause.
corrected_fix: Add a module-level generation counter. In switchPack: const gen = ++switchGen at entry; after every await (each loadPack attempt and the 600ms retry sleep), bail if gen !== switchGen || live, and if the disc was already built when bailing, dispose it before returning. In startRecording: bump switchGen (++switchGen) before/after the status fetch so any in-flight switchPack invalidates itself, and keep its own current-cleanup. The COMPLETE handler needs no separate check beyond calling the now-guarded switchPack, but its await fetchPacks() should also be followed by a live re-check. Optionally, as defense in depth, make the entry cleanup idempotent by removing/disposing via a helper that both switchPack and startRecording share.

summary: gl_PointSize = clamp(px, 1.0, 8.0) defeats the 4096px export: exportStill sets uPointScale = 4096/2.04 ≈ 2008 so notes should be ~27px and grains ~15px, but every point is capped at 8 device pixels, so the archival PNG has marks 2-3.4x thinner relative to the disc than intended.
scenario: Operator presses 'PNG 4K'. export-still.js:15 sets uPointScale = size/2.04 = 2007.8 (device px per world unit, matching the ±1.02 ortho camera). Shader: note px = 2007.8 * 0.0135 = 27.1 → clamped to 8; grain px = 15.1 → 8. Meanwhile the alpha gain clamp(uPointScale/700, 0.55, 3.5) = 2.87 still applies, boosting per-point alpha as if the points had grown. Result: the print/archive export does not match the on-screen artwork — engraving is far finer and additive saturation is concentrated into 8px dots (and 1px GL line strokes shrink relative to the disc as well). The whole point of the 4096 target — print quality at the on-screen density — is silently lost.
repro_evidence: Arithmetic against the actual constants in shaders.js:46-47 and export-still.js:7,15; no GPU needed — clamp(2007.8*0.0135, 1, 8) = 8 vs intended 27.1.
fix_sketch: Raise or bypass the size clamp during export — e.g. add a uMaxPointPx uniform (8 on screen, ~64 or size-proportional for export; keep within gl.ALIASED_POINT_SIZE_RANGE), or clamp px relative to uPointScale so the cap scales with resolution.
reasoning: Verified by reading /Users/mehmetunal/Documents/CluadeCodeFiles/2000-traces/viz/src/shaders.js:46-47 and export-still.js:15 plus the on-screen scale path (main.js:232-233, scene.js:78). Export sets uPointScale = 4096/2.04 = 2007.84; the shader computes note px = 2007.84*0.0135 = 27.11 and grain px = 15.06, but gl_PointSize = clamp(px, 1.0, 8.0) caps both at 8 device pixels on the 4096 target. On screen, uPointScale = (viewH/2)*zoom*pixelRatio ≈ 414-920 at fit view, so marks are unclamped (or only mildly clamped) and occupy 0.44-0.68% of the disc diameter, versus 0.20% in the export — the claimed 2-3.4x relative thinning is arithmetically exact (27.1/8 = 3.39 worst case). Meanwhile shaders.js:37's exposure gain clamp(uPointScale/700, 0.55, 3.5) = 2.87 still applies during export, concentrating near-maximum per-point alpha into 8px dots, so the additive look diverges from screen in both size and saturation. The secondary stroke observation is also true (WebGL LineSegments rasterize at 1 device px regardless of target size), though that part is an API limitation not caused by this clamp. Export-still.js's own header ("print/archive quality") and the deliberate size-proportional uPointScale show the resolution-scaled intent that the hardcoded 8.0 silently defeats. No GPU repro needed: the failure is pure arithmetic on compile-time shader constants.
corrected_fix: Add a uMaxPointPx uniform to DISC_VERTEX and use gl_PointSize = clamp(px, 1.0, uMaxPointPx). Set it to 8.0 for interactive rendering (disc.js/live-disc.js defaults) and raise it in exportStill proportionally to resolution (e.g. 8.0 * (size/2.04) / typicalScreenScale, or simply ~32-64 for size=4096, staying within gl.ALIASED_POINT_SIZE_RANGE, which is >=1024 on desktop GPUs so 27px is safe; save/restore it alongside uPointScale/uTime/uSelLane). This lets the export's px = 27.1 (notes) / 15.1 (grains) render at intended size, and the alpha gain at shaders.js:37 then matches appearance again. Note the 1-device-px LineSegments strokes will still be relatively thin at 4096 — that is a WebGL lineWidth limitation and would need quad/mesh-based strokes to fix, out of scope for this finding.

summary: exportStill neutralizes uTime/uSelLane/uPointScale but not uReplaying or the playhead material, so exporting while a replay is in progress (even paused mid-scrub) bakes a bright radial playhead line and a 'fresh glow' hot wedge into the archival PNG.
scenario: Natural flow: operator scrubs to an interesting moment (onSeek pauses the transport), then clicks 'PNG 4K'. summary: Drag state machine never resets on pointercancel/context-menu, and pointerdown accepts any button, so one right-click leaves the view in a permanent 'pan follows the mouse with no button held' state.

summary: A crash/power-cut mid-write leaves a half JSON line at EOF, and both packSession (viz-pack.js:29) and importSession (jsonl.js:19) do a bare JSON.parse per line, so the advertised crash-recovery property of the recorder ('a crash mid-run leaves a valid partial JSONL file') fails at exactly the moment it matters.

Truncation mid-line is genuinely reachable: power loss persists the page cache at block granularity, and ENOSPC can partially complete a write before recorder.js's writeError path gives up — the recorder's finally-block flush cannot make the kernel-level cut land on a line boundary. Repro at tmp-repro/repro-truncated.js: an intact 2-event file packs fine (2 events); the same file cut 25 bytes before EOF makes packSession throw SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input (readline emits the final partial line even without a trailing newline), and importSession throws the same. Minor overstatements in the claim: recovery is a one-line sed to drop the last line, not hex surgery, and a plain SIGKILL alone usually leaves a line-aligned file since each line is written as one whole chunk (power-cut/ENOSPC/partial-write+kill are the reliable triggers); the exact SyntaxError message also differs (position-dependent). Neither affects the core finding.
corrected_fix: In both line loops, tolerate a JSON.parse failure only on the final non-empty line of the file: since lines stream lazily, hold a failed line in a pending slot and rethrow if any subsequent non-empty line arrives; if the failure was on the last line, treat it as an EOF truncation, drop it, and surface it in stats/logs (e.g. truncatedTail: true). Apply to packSession (viz-pack.js:27-38) and importSession (jsonl.js:17-24); a mid-file corrupt line must still throw. Optionally have the viz-pack CLI print a clear "salvaged truncated tail" note so operators know the pack is from a crashed take.

summary: The render loop overwrites the rec-button label every frame, so '■ DURDURULUYOR…' never appears and the entire FINALIZING/packing phase (seconds to tens of seconds for 2.7M events) is displayed as a still-active recording.

summary: startRecording is re-entrant: `live` is only assigned after an awaited /api/status fetch and no feedback is shown until then, so a second KAYIT click opens a second EventSource — every batch is then appended twice (doubled grains/counts) and the first EventSource leaks forever, contaminating later takes.

The second click sees `live` still null (main.js:47) and runs startRecording concurrently: two EventSources are created, both delivering every /api/live broadcast into the shared module-level `live` object, so processLiveEvents appends each event twice — grainCount and the additive-blended brightness are doubled on the projection. stopLiveUi closes only `live.es` (the second ES); the first stays subscribed in the server's liveClients forever, and on the NEXT take its frames are processed again alongside the new connection, doubling that take too.

Scope caveat supporting 'important' rather than 'critical': only the live projection view is corrupted — the JSONL/pack recording happens server-side in recorder.js and is unaffected, and a page reload clears the leak.

Defensively close any prior EventSource before creating a new one (`live?.es?.close()`), and have the onRecord handler treat the connecting state as 'already starting' rather than routing to stopRecording.

summary: A failed recording is invisible on the operator panel: /api/status flips to IDLE and silently reverts stats/participants to the PREVIOUS take's numbers (status has no error field, and the error is only broadcast on /api/live, which ui/index.html never listens to).
scenario: Take 1 succeeds (2 participants, 3 stored). Take 2's upstream SSE fails (auth revoked / LAN drop). The record promise rejects, phase goes to IDLE, and status() falls back to lastSummary — the panel then shows DURUM: IDLE with KATILIMCI 2 and KAYITLI OLAY 3 from the previous take, with no error indication whatsoever. An operator glancing at the panel sees plausible session numbers and can believe the take landed; the only hint is the state quietly returning to IDLE.
fix_sketch: Add `lastError` to createControlServer, set it in the .catch, expose it in status() (and clear it on the next start); render it prominently in ui/index.html. Also null out the stats/participants fallback after a failure so the panel doesn't show a dead take's numbers.

HOWEVER, the claim's trigger is wrong: an upstream SSE failure (auth revoked / LAN drop) does NOT reject the record promise in the production wiring. server.js:201 builds liveSource with default maxRetries=Infinity (live-source.js:7), which retries forever; the durationMs+5000 killer abort makes the generator return cleanly (live-source.js:30) and recordFromSource resolves — repro Part B shows the panel then ends at COMPLETE with take 2's own honest numbers (participants 0, stored 0) and lastSummary overwritten, not stale take-1 numbers. The confirmed invisible-failure path is instead reached by: (a) an async disk-write error mid-take (ENOSPC/EACCES — recorder.js:24-29,39 rethrows and rejects; sessions reach ~2.7M events so this is a real hazard), or (b) packSession throwing inside the .then handler (server.js:100-103), which chains into the same .catch after a fully successful recording (JSONL on disk, but panel shows IDLE + previous take's numbers and no pack). So: mechanism and summary confirmed; the specific SSE-failure narrative refuted; severity kept at important because a silent failure masquerading as the previous good take's numbers on a live-show operator panel is an operational hazard, though the realistic trigger frequency is lower than the claim implies.
corrected_fix: In createControlServer (src/server.js): add a `lastError` variable; set it in the record .catch (e.g. { message: err?.message ?? 'recording failed', sessionId, at: Date.now() }) and clear it in POST /api/start; include it in status() output; in the .catch, do NOT leave lastSummary as the previous take's numbers backing status() — either clear lastSummary or add a lastError-aware fallback so stats/participants read 0/null after a failed take. Render lastError prominently in ui/index.html's tick(). Note the trigger correction: this path fires on disk-write errors (ENOSPC/EACCES) and autoPack packSession failures — for pack failures, consider setting phase to COMPLETE-with-error instead of IDLE since the JSONL recording itself succeeded. Upstream SSE failures never reach this path (liveSource retries forever, then resolves as an empty COMPLETE take); if upstream death should be visible mid-take, surface liveSource reconnect state separately (e.g. an onSourceStall/onRetry tap broadcast into status), which is outside this .catch.

summary: During FINALIZING `current` is already null and lastSummary is still the previous run, so /api/status reports state FINALIZING with the PREVIOUS session's sessionId, stats, participants and packName; /api/stop in the same window answers 409 'not recording' despite the FINALIZING state.
scenario: Session A completed earlier; session B (large, e.g. 2.7M events) finishes and the server awaits packSession for seconds. Any /api/status poll in that window returns {state:'FINALIZING', sessionId:<A>, stats:<A's>, packName:'kayit-<A>'} — a panel keyed on sessionId shows the wrong session finalizing with wrong numbers, and an operator pressing stop in that window is told 'not recording' with no hint that finalization is in progress.
fix_sketch: Keep a `finalizing = { sessionId, stats, participants }` snapshot (taken from summary before `current = null`) and have status() prefer it while phase==='FINALIZING'; make /api/stop return a phase-accurate message (e.g. 409 'finalizing').
repro_evidence: Instrumented poll run: state transitions seen were RECORDING(sessionId B) -> FINALIZING(sessionId A, stats {received:1} from A, packName kayit-A) for ~250 consecutive polls -> COMPLETE(sessionId B). Deterministic from code: .then sets current=null before phase='FINALIZING' and only sets lastSummary after `await packSession`.

In src/server.js the record .then handler sets current=null (line 95) before phase='FINALIZING' (line 96), and lastSummary is only updated at line 104 after `await packSession(...)` (line 102). status() (lines 52-58) falls back to lastSummary for stats/participants/sessionId/packName whenever current is null, so every /api/status call during the pack reports state FINALIZING paired with the PREVIOUS session's sessionId, stats, participants, and packName. packSession (viz-pack.js:21) is async and streams the whole JSONL line-by-line, so for large sessions the window lasts seconds. /api/stop (line 118) checks only `!current` and returns 409 'not recording' in that same window, unlike /api/arm whose 409 message is phase-accurate. Repro (tmp-repro/finalizing-status-repro.mjs): after a 50-event session A, a 400k-event session B finished and auto-packed; 122 consecutive status polls during B's pack returned {state:'FINALIZING', sessionId:<A>, stats:{received:50}, participants:50, packName:'kayit-<A>'} and /api/stop returned 409 {"error":"not recording"}, then status flipped to COMPLETE with B's correct data. Caveats that keep it minor: the window is only observable when autoPack && packsDir && participants>0 (the production direct-run entrypoint does set autoPack:true), the wrong-session data needs a prior completed session (first run shows sessionId:null instead), and nothing is corrupted — recording and packing are unaffected; it is an operator-panel status/UX defect.
corrected_fix: In src/server.js's record .then handler, capture a finalizing snapshot before clearing current: `finalizing = { sessionId, stats: summary.stats, participants: summary.participants }; current = null; phase = 'FINALIZING';` and clear it (finalizing = null) when setting lastSummary/phase='COMPLETE' and in the .catch. Have status() prefer it: when phase==='FINALIZING' and current is null, report the snapshot's sessionId/stats/participants and packName:null (or the in-progress pack name). Make /api/stop phase-aware: if !current, return 409 with `cannot stop from ${phase}` (e.g. 'finalizing') instead of the blanket 'not recording'.

summary: There is no way to leave ARMED: /api/stop requires `current` (only set by start) and returns 409 'not recording', /api/arm from ARMED returns 409, so an accidental arm can only be undone by recording and completing a junk session.
scenario: Operator arms too early during pre-show (or a UI double-click arms at the wrong moment). The panel now shows ARMED; stop returns 409 'not recording', re-arm returns 409 'cannot arm from ARMED'. The only way back to IDLE is to hit start and let a throwaway session run to completion (or wall-clock kill after durationMs+5s), leaving a junk JSONL and, with autoPack, a junk pack in the viz index.
fix_sketch: Add a disarm path: either accept POST /api/stop in ARMED (phase='IDLE', broadcast state IDLE) or add POST /api/disarm guarded on phase==='ARMED'.
repro_evidence: Code read of the handlers map (server.js:61-140): arm requires phase IDLE|COMPLETE, stop requires current!=null, and no other handler mutates phase — no transition out of ARMED exists except start.
reasoning: Code read of src/server.js:61-140 confirms the transition gap: POST /api/arm requires phase IDLE|COMPLETE (409 from ARMED), POST /api/stop requires current != null which only /api/start sets (409 'not recording' in ARMED), and phase is a closure-local mutated only at lines 65/96/105/111/114 — the sole exit from ARMED is /api/start. A runtime repro (tmp-repro/armed-stuck.mjs, dummy abortable source) reproduced it live: arm → ARMED; stop → 409 {"error":"not recording"}; re-arm → 409 {"error":"cannot arm from ARMED"}; state stays ARMED. One overstatement in the scenario: escaping does NOT require running a throwaway session to completion or waiting durationMs+5s — start followed by immediate stop resolves in milliseconds because controller.abort() makes liveSource return cleanly (live-source.js:30), so the record promise resolves and phase reaches COMPLETE, from which re-arm succeeds. That escape still leaves a junk 2-line JSONL in sessionsDir (repro-verified); a junk pack is only produced if the pre-show feed delivered events in the brief window before abort (server.js:100 guards autoPack on participants > 0 — the repro's empty session produced no pack). Restarting the panel process (in-memory phase) is the only artifact-free escape. The defect stands: no legitimate disarm exists, and the workaround pollutes the sessions dir mid-show-prep. Severity 'minor' is appropriate given the cheap, fast workaround.
corrected_fix: Add a disarm path in src/server.js. Simplest: in the 'POST /api/stop' handler, branch before the !current check — if (phase === 'ARMED') { phase = 'IDLE'; broadcast({ kind: 'state', state: 'IDLE' }); return json(res, status()); } — keeping the existing 409 for other non-recording phases. Alternatively add a dedicated 'POST /api/disarm' handler guarded on phase === 'ARMED' with the same body. Either way, broadcast the IDLE state so /api/live viewers and the panel resync.

summary: frame() overwrites the KAYIT button label every frame while live.disc exists, so the '■ DURDURULUYOR…' (and '■ KAYIT') states set elsewhere are never visible — the operator gets zero feedback that their stop click registered.
scenario: During a recording, stopRecording sets '■ DURDURULUYOR…' (main.js:142); the very next requestAnimationFrame tick replaces it with the time/grain counter (main.js:242) because live.disc is truthy. The operator sees no change after clicking stop and either clicks repeatedly or doubts the system while the ~1-2s FINALIZING pass runs. Same for the '■ KAYIT' label set at main.js:172/190.
fix_sketch: Render the time/grain counter into the stats element (hud.setStats) instead of the rec button, or track a 'stopping' flag in live and skip the per-frame setRecState while it is set.
reasoning: frame() (main.js:228-246) re-queues itself unconditionally and, whenever live?.disc is truthy, writes the time/grain counter into the rec button via hud.setRecState (main.js:242 → hud.js:75-78, which sets $('rec').textContent). stopRecording() (main.js:141-144) sets '■ DURDURULUYOR…' on that same button but does not clear live or live.disc — teardown happens only in stopLiveUi(), which handleLive() calls only on 'COMPLETE' or 'IDLE'+error (main.js:191-204); the FINALIZING state is not handled at all. So during the entire finalize window live.disc stays truthy and line 242 repaints the counter every rAF tick (~16ms), leaving the stop label visible for at most one frame. Worse, once recording stops no more batches advance live.maxT or the grain count, so the button shows a frozen counter visually identical to the pre-click state — the operator gets no perceptible feedback that stop registered, and the still-enabled button invites repeat clicks (harmless re-POSTs of /api/stop). The '■ KAYIT' half of the claim is also mechanically true (in the normal path the hello carries a roster, so ensureLiveDisc at main.js:170 runs before the setRecState at 172, and the label is overwritten next frame), though it is cosmetically moot since the per-frame counter itself shows '■' plus a running clock; only in the no-roster-yet path (live.disc null) does that label persist, so "never visible" is slightly overstated for that half. The core defect — stop feedback invisible during FINALIZING — genuinely occurs in the current code.
corrected_fix: Either (a) set a flag in stopRecording() — e.g. live.stopping = true — and guard the per-frame overwrite at main.js:242 with `if (!live.stopping) hud.setRecState(...)` so '■ DURDURULUYOR…' persists through FINALIZING; or (b) cleaner: move the live time/grain counter into hud.setStats() so the rec button exclusively displays state labels ('● KAYIT' / '● BAĞLANIYOR…' / '■ KAYIT' / '■ DURDURULUYOR…'). Optionally also handle the unhandled 'FINALIZING' state message in handleLive() to set the stopping label from the server-side transition as well.

summary: On a fresh install with no packs, fetchPacks falls back to FALLBACK_PACKS = ['live-2000', 'loadgen-384'] — packs that do not exist — so boot shows 'paket yüklenemedi: live-2000' and the HUD select offers two phantom entries.
scenario: Fresh checkout, no recordings yet: /packs/index.json is missing, Vite's SPA fallback serves index.html with 200, r.json() throws, catch returns the fallback list. switchPack('live-2000') fails twice (manifest fetch also gets HTML) and the operator lands on an error with a dropdown of two selectable packs that both fail. Additionally, if the index fetch races/fails right after a recording COMPLETEs, hud.setPacks(FALLBACK, packName) selects a value with no matching option, leaving the select displaying the wrong pack name.
fix_sketch: Drop FALLBACK_PACKS (return []) and render an explicit empty state ('henüz kayıt yok — KAYIT ile başla'); guard switchPack/setPacks against an empty list; in the COMPLETE handler, append packName to PACKS if the refetched index does not contain it yet.
repro_evidence: viz/public/packs listing shows those two packs exist only in this working copy as prior recordings; nothing generates them on a clean deploy. Fallback path traced through fetchPacks (main.js:14-19) and switchPack (main.js:96-102).

(1) viz/public/packs/ is gitignored, so a fresh checkout has no packs; (2) Vite's SPA fallback serves index.html with 200 text/html even for missing .json paths (repro output: status=200 type=text/html for /packs/does-not-exist-index.json and /packs/no-such-pack/manifest.json), so fetchPacks (main.js:14-19) passes the r.ok check, r.json() throws on HTML, and the catch returns FALLBACK_PACKS = ['live-2000','loadgen-384'] (main.js:12); (3) loadPack (pack-loader.js:8) has no r.ok check, also receives 200 HTML, throws; switchPack (main.js:97-102) retries once then shows 'paket yüklenemedi: live-2000'; boot calls switchPack(PACKS[0]) at main.js:264; (4) the HUD select (hud.js:59-63) is populated with both phantom names and both fail when chosen; (5) nothing regenerates those names — auto-pack names are 'kayit-<timestamp>' (server.js:101), and live-2000/loadgen-384 exist only in this working copy. The secondary COMPLETE-race scenario is weaker than claimed: server.js:102-106 awaits packSession (which updates index.json) before broadcasting COMPLETE, so only a transient fetch failure triggers it, and a non-matching select value renders blank (selectedIndex -1), not 'the wrong pack name'. These details do not affect the primary finding.
